claim_scope: Historical investigation of experimental question change; discriminates first-person source, edited diary indexes, secondary interpretive theses and failed observations.

records.event: Transient induction effects on closing/opening battery circuit via ring
records.witness: edited Diary first volume index; early entry in public preview
records.inference: initial success and immediate perturbation constraint
records.limit: diary index/edited quotation are not a handwritten manuscript witness

records.event: First Series presented to Royal Society; Faraday states results deliberately not narrated in discovery order
records.witness: Faraday First Series section 1 paras 1-5 in publisher public excerpt
records.inference: published rhetorical order is not equivalent to experimental chronology
records.limit: a contemporary authored publication is distinct from laboratory diary; printed 1832

records.event: Index lists varied induction tests, earth magnetism and loop movement; later elementary experiment must be checked
records.witness: edited Diary table of contents pp. 400-407, section 274
records.inference: candidate shift from apparatus-specific testing to systematic general rule
records.limit: full dated primary entry text/handwriting not read; Steinle 1997 supports secondary interpretation

records.event: Parallel long copper/iron wires aligned to Earth's magnetic meridian, reported as failed
records.witness: Faraday Correspondence editorial note linked to 1832 Jan6 letter
records.limit: editor's reconstruction from Diary; physical setup not independently reconstructed

records.event: Faraday schedules further pond experiment with John S. Acton
records.witness: Faraday first-person letter (RI MS) through Epsilon transcription
records.inference: documents planned experiment independently of later success narrative
records.limit: letter is schedule, not an outcome record

records.event: Kensington pond circuit attempt without expected effect
records.witness: Epsilon historical editor note citing Faraday Diary
records.inference: negative case against teleological all-success narrative
records.limit: secondary summary; original Diary pages 293-302 not yet reviewed

records.event: Waterloo Bridge long-wire current experiment: no satisfactory result
records.witness: Epsilon editor note citing Faraday Diary and reports
records.inference: negative case; failure does not by itself reveal exact cause
records.limit: no full apparatus or notebook data audited

competing_interpretations: Theory proposes a target then experimental system monotonically verifies it.
Prior speculation motivates an early experiment, an unexpected transient effect expands exploratory variation, later paper reorganizes findings into explanatory form.
Apparatus/instrumentation trajectory and historical concept work are inseparable; conventional Steinle narrative already explains important transitions.
comparison.discriminator: To adjudicate, compare dated diary question formulations, modifications of apparatus, failures and retrospective editorial wording. Do not infer discovery causation from publication sequence.
comparison.positive_scope: Question repertoire and experiment menu can be revised even when no new formal equation appears.

remaining_work: Read complete dated December 23-26 1831 Diary original text or an authenticated critical facsimile, with precise volume/page concordance.
Read original January 10 and 12-13 1832 diary entries, compare editorial note to Faraday's exact wording.
Compare November 1831 submitted original or final 1832 First Series and 1832 Second Series sections with contemporaneous diary order.
Run explicit Bell 1969/1972 contrast: written theory-guided test vs Faraday's mixed guided-exploratory pathway.
Compare at least one independent Steinle rival and a primary negative case before generalizing.
